title: Retry context & granular status mapping for resumable streaming in SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a cross-language, ergonomic error & retry model for streaming RPCs and long-running generation streams. Deliver: (1) a small set of granular canonical statuses mapped to HTTP/gRPC/transport-layer errors, (2) per-error actionable retry hints (backoff, idempotency, resume token), and (3) language-specific ergonomics (Python/TypeScript/Go) to make resuming and retrying safe and obvious for application authors.
background: We've had multiple customer and internal incidents where clients either indefinitely retried non-idempotent streams or gave up on recoverable network blips. Existing SDK errors are inconsistent across languages and lack machine-readable retry guidance. Previous tickets focused on unifying error codes for unary calls; this ticket targets streaming flows which have different constraints (KV cache, partial outputs, resume tokens).
proposal_summary: Introduce a compact status taxonomy and attach a RetryHint object to streaming errors. RetryHint fields: category (transient|permanent|rate_limit|auth|overloaded|resumable), recommended_backoff_ms, max_retries, idempotent_hint, resume_token (optional). Expose language-idiomatic surfaces: Python exceptions with attributes, TypeScript Error subclass with .retryHint and .resume(), Go sentinel errors with helpers (errors.Is/Unwrap + RetryHint struct). Implement mapping from transport (HTTP 5xx, 429, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, CANCELLED, etc.) to taxonomy and populate hints in the runtime before surface to SDKs.
technical_design: Canonical statuses: TRANSIENT, PERMANENT, RATE_LIMIT, AUTH, OVERLOADED, CANCELLED, RESUMABLE
Transport mapping rules: map HTTP 502/503/504 + gRPC UNAVAILABLE->TRANSIENT; 429->RATE_LIMIT; 401/403->AUTH; 400/409->PERMANENT (unless payload-truncated); client-cancel->CANCELLED
RetryHint schema (string fields stored as JSON in telemetry and surfaced as typed objects in SDKs): category, recommended_backoff_ms, max_retries, idempotent (true|false), resume_token

Python ergonomic surface: raise StreamResumeError(message) with attributes .retry_hint (dict), .resume_token (str|None). Provide helper redwood.stream_resume(stream, token) to continue consumption without re-fetching full context.

TypeScript ergonomic surface: export class StreamError extends Error { retryHint?: RetryHint; resumeToken?: string; resume(client): Promise<Stream> }, provide a typed resume API to reduce user boilerplate.

Go ergonomic surface: define type StreamErr struct { Msg string; Hint RetryHint } implementing error; provide helper functions ResumeToken(err error) (string, bool) and ShouldRetry(err error) (bool, RetryPolicy).

Runtime behavior: on server-side detection of partial-progressable state, issue a resumable error code with resume_token. Add deterministic resume-token format: base64(prefix:stream_id:offset:signature) to validate on server and prevent mismatch exploits.
Telemetry: log reason, retry_hint fields, and client language+version. Emit metrics for resume_success_rate and retry_replay_ratio.
Backward compatibility: if client library doesn't understand RetryHint, include human-readable message and a short machine-parsable 'retry_meta' header in responses.
Docs: add a migration guide for existing SDK users and example patterns for safe retries with side effects (idempotency keys, at-least-once concerns).
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose the RetryHint schema and make resume_token discoverable on streaming errors
Runtime emits RetryHint for mapped transport errors in canary environments (internal test cluster)
Unit + integration tests cover: transient retries, rate_limit backoff, resume flow with partial output, and non-retry of permanent errors
E2E chaos test: simulated network interruptions for long-running generation stream with >= 95% successful resume in controlled load
Developer docs and three language examples live in docs.sdk/errors/resumable-streams.md
No breaking API contract for unary endpoints (existing unary error behavior preserved)
Telemetry pipeline receives retry_hint fields and the resume_success_rate dashboard shows expected signals
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): design doc and prototype runtime mapping; add RetryHint proto/json representation; create resume_token format proposal
Phase 2 (2w): implement runtime population of RetryHint; wire telemetry; internal canary with Python SDK consuming RetryHint
Phase 3 (2w): implement TypeScript and Go SDK surfaces, add helpers and examples
Phase 4 (1w): tests, docs, and rollout gating; soft launch on a subset of customers and internal teams
Phase 5 (ongoing): monitor metrics, iterate on backoff defaults and idempotency guidance
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping table (transport -> category + default_backoff)
Integration tests: resume_token validation and resume handshake across simulated server restarts
Property tests: fuzz resume_token parsing and signature validation
Chaos/injection: drop TCP packets and force client reconnects to validate resume success rate
Language acceptance: run example apps in Python/TS/Go with the SDKs and verify ergonomic helpers behave as documented
blockers: finalizing resume_token signing algorithm (security review requested)
backward-compatibility decision for old clients that ignore retry_meta header
